posts.name: Raccoonoo
posts.cooked:
I think the dissonance between card game strength and comic book strength is showing with both Gloomweaver, who managed to pressure both the Prime Wardens and Visionary to the point that Vanessa was overcome by Darkmind, and Chokepoint, who stomped The Sentinels and the Termi-Nation heroes with her really useful metal powers.

That said, I was simultaneously surprised and hyped up by Dawn and Progeny's fight. I thought people were overestimating Dawn when they said she was powerful enough to take out a monster that had systematically dismantled most of the earth's heroes and, even if Progeny wasn't quite at full power, I'm happy that I was proven wrong.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
I too made most of my decisions based on what would make for a cool story rather than who would beat whom in a fair fight.  That was mostly due to my misconception that this would be a magazine, with 2-3 battles per issue, with lots of time for talking.  I didn't think it could be a single book since it would have to be hundreds of pages to do them any kind of justice.  Once I realized that, most of what I would have found surprising (not having Ra vs. Fanatic, Setback vs. Expatriette) made much more sense.

I figured The Operative would beat Fright Train.  His armor isn't one solid piece, it has gaps, and she'd find them.  I did not expect Plague Rat's infection to have an impact on that fight, since Revocorp cured Plague Rat of his infectiousness, and it only came back in the Miststorm timeline.

Like so many others, I thought Bugbear would feed off the Proletariats and grow stronger.  Seems he was the only one to not get at least some sort of explanation and incentive to fight before being tossed in.

Biomancer vs. Isis was a big one for me.  I had no idea he could transmute himself.  I figured that, like the Chairman, he'd bow out as quickly as he could manage.

I know lots of folks expected Citizen Dawn to beat Progeny, but I wasn't one of them.  In Progeny's original form, the only way to beat him (in the comics) is to exploit the weaknesses he creates in himself when he adapts to attack forms.  Dawn only has one attack form.  The fact that he was both in a weakened state and effectively solar-powered changed this completely.

And, of course, Benchmark in general.  The fact that the writers of Cosmic Contest were at odds with the writers of Benchmark's other appearances threw me off completely.  I expected him to do far better.  Writhe, too; he's supposed to rely heavily on inventions, but didn't use them at all, so I didn't expect him to be a one-trick pony (nor so dumb as to try to enter an absolute-zero environment suit).

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
We guessed Nightmist would win because we assumed she had to learn something to discover what she needed to do to deal with OblivAeon. We thought she's learn it from Jansa, though, but it worked out. 

We really couldn't imagine Unity taking out Omnitron-U, so that was a shock. We also couldn't imagine Haka reaching Ra, as others described (and we saw a Ra vs. Fanatic confrontation as an interesting one), or that Stuntman could take that level of abuse. 

On the flip side, we didn’t realize Chrono-Ranger could bounce around like that! We also forgot we were dealing with Dark Visionary, which makes a big difference. And we assumed Plague Rat’s venom would work against Fright Train – turns out it was too slow to do what we expected it to do. 

But none of that do I blame on anyone but us in our analysis.   It was all good fun!

I like that Benchmark lost so quickly. The fact that he was created solely to be the new best superhero without irony is a thing that happens a lot in comics. The minds behind the “totally fictional” Sentinel Comics wanted a new character to be the most popular. New toys, movies, thousands of comics and appearances. So the writers were forced to make Benchmark outmaneuver Tachyon, lead better than Legacy, and take a punch from Haka. In the comic universe, he shows up and just outshines everyone. 

Based on the quick summary of in the podcast, that’s why he was created. I also find these kind of characters are just so annoying. Having him lose is a good screw you to the “higher ups”. Reminds me of the Uncanny X-men storyline of Fear Itself with Adam the X-Treme. Source: https://static.comicvine.com/uploads/original/10/102687/1968063-adam_x.jpg
